summary: Columbia County, OR lookout built 1934; staffed by couples to 1951; duties moved to Clatskanie Mountain in 1954; structure removed, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Pole platform with ground cabin (40 ft per the register and firelookout); a 1942 inspection describes a 45-foot tower with a 7x7 cab and a 12x16 ground cabin
facts.status_note: Structure removed; the sources do not date its removal

staffing.status: Staffed by George and Mrs. Jones in 1942-45 and by Chester Hall and his wife in 1950-51; duties moved to Clatskanie Mountain in 1954

visit.trail_note: No structure remains to climb; no source describes the site today or public access

events.note: 40-foot pole platform and ground cabin, per the register and firelookout. A March 1935 Forest Log note describes establishing a secondary lookout on Benson Mountain.
May 1942 inspection: 45-foot tower with 7x7 cab and 12x16 ground cabin

Chester Hall and his wife manned their old post again after moving back in 1950
Duties transferred to the new lookout on Clatskanie Mountain
Registered September 22, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout give 40 feet (about 12.2 m). The 1942 inspection quoted by Forest Lookouts gives 45 feet. The record keeps 13.7 m (45 ft) because the inspection describes the structure in detail.
The register and firelookout date the platform to 1934. A March 1935 Forest Log note describes establishing the secondary lookout. The story uses the 1934 register date and reports the 1935 note.

notes_for_editor: Brief had access unknown; no access level is set because no source describes public access. The Clatskanie Mountain tower is a separate replacement structure (US 679), not the Benson tower. Source [4] is a personal blog, used only for the replacement's history and location. The 1942 inspection (45 ft) and the register (40 ft) disagree on height; the brief's 13.7 m follows the 45 ft figure. No photos added.
